data.title: Trust Me, I'm Local: Chrome Extensions, MCP, and the Sandbox Escape
data.author: el_duderino
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Chrome扩展程序与本地MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务器交互所带来的严重安全风险。MCP服务器通常缺乏身份验证机制，导致任何Chrome扩展可以在无需特殊权限的情况下访问本地资源，甚至可能完全接管机器。文章描述了一个实例：一个Chrome扩展与本地MCP服务器通信，未经认证即可操作文件系统等敏感资源。由于Chrome的沙箱模型无法阻止这种攻击，用户面临极大的安全威胁。文章呼吁开发者和用户重新评估本地MCP服务器的安全性，以防止潜在的灾难性后果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chrome扩展和MCP（以及更广泛的应用程序）在本地服务器连接和安全方面的潜在风险与解决方案

不同观点：
• telotortium认为，文章提到的问题与MCP没有直接关系，而是Chrome扩展本身可以通过localhost端口进行HTTP连接，只要有服务器运行即可，且扩展已经需要权限才能与localhost通信。
• vovkasm指出，尽管与MCP无关，但操作系统缺乏对本地TCP连接的便捷且可靠的访问控制机制，这导致用户无法方便地控制哪些应用可以连接到特定本地端口，类似问题也存在于其他本地服务器应用程序中。
• fluffet从历史角度出发，认为当前的AI工具忽略了早期互联网协议已经学习到的安全教训，强调需要监管和更稳健的协议设计。
• npace12介绍了自己开发的"little-rat" Chrome扩展，它可以跟踪和阻止其他扩展的流量，以此作为应对措施。
• bhelx建议将MCP服务器运行在沙盒环境中，尤其是使用WASM技术，这样可以提高安全性，并提到可以通过SSE传输数据。
• OsrsNeedsf2P提出，MCP可能因为没有安全摩擦而击败了其他竞争对手，暗示安全性可能不是其成功的关键因素。
• skybrian认为，“允许连接到localhost”的权限过于宽泛，用户很难据此做出明智的安全决策，建议本地服务器应加入认证机制。
• ramoz表示，当前所谓的“新零日AI漏洞”实际上只是暴露了标准安全实践中的老问题，强调本地应用开放连接和没有CORS限制本身就存在风险。
• happyopossum指出，问题与MCP无关，任何监听localhost的应用都可能面临类似风险，扩展只是利用了这些漏洞。
• fpoling建议，本地运行的服务应该拒绝带有Origin头的HTTP请求，以及通常拒绝带有UserAgent的请求，以此作为一种防护手段。
• babyshake询问是否使用streamable HTTP MCP服务器可以避免某些漏洞，并讨论了STDIO/SSE的必要性。
• brap质疑为何需要新的协议（如MCP），认为现有的OpenAPI规范已经足够，且支持广泛的API和认证机制。
• olalonde提出了具体的解决方案问题，询问是通过在MCP服务器上添加认证机制，还是通过Chrome限制未经授权的localhost调用来解决安全问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于MCP是否是问题的核心，还是这只是更广泛的Chrome扩展和本地服务器安全问题的一部分。
• 一些参与者（如vovkasm、skybrian）强调了操作系统或浏览器应提供更好的访问控制机制，而其他人（如ramoz、happyopossum）则认为这并非新问题，只是现有安全风险的延伸。
• 提出了多种技术解决方案，如使用WASM、加入认证机制、拒绝特定HTTP请求等，但尚未达成一致意见。
• 部分讨论也涉及AI工具和协议的设计是否忽视了早期的安全教训，呼吁更稳健的协议和监管措施。

Trust Me, I’m Local: Chrome Extensions, MCP, and the Sandbox Escape
Yuval Ronen
Follow
6 min read
·
Apr 24, 2025
--
Listen
Share
Let’s talk about MCPs. You’ve probably heard of them, and maybe you’ve read the security risks associated with them. Sure, they sound worrying, but when you put them into a real-world context, they can quickly become far more concerning than you can ever imagine.
Just last week, our system flagged a suspicious Chrome extension. It sent messages to a port on localhost — nothing too odd at first glance, but as we dug deeper, we found that this extension communicated with an MCP server running on the local machine.
The fact that Chrome extensions can communicate with MCPs is a serious risk. The consequences are enormous. The usual security measures like Chrome’s sandbox model, don’t stand a chance.
You’re looking at unauthenticated access to the filesystem and, in some cases, a full machine takeover. That’s not just a small issue;
that’s a massive, game-changing vulnerability.
And here’s the kicker:
any
Chrome extension can exploit this. No special permissions required. If there’s a vulnerable MCP server running on a host machine, that’s it. We’ve already found vulnerable MCP servers tied to services like filesystem access, Slack, WhatsApp, and more. This isn’t just a theoretical risk anymore, it’s real, and the impact could be devastating.
So, if you’re running MCP locally, it’s time to seriously reevaluate your security. We were mindblown when we found this, and it’s time everyone else takes notice before it’s too late.
So, buckle up and get ready, let’s dive into this together.
A Suspicious localhost connection
While monitoring browser extension activity, our detection engine flagged a Chrome extension making network requests to localhost. Although the extension itself showed no signs of malicious behavior, the destination caught our attention. It was communicating with a local service implementing the
Model Context Protocol (MCP)
— a protocol used to interface AI agents with system tools and resources on the endpoint.
localhost MCP connection from chrome extension
This raised an immediate concern: if a browser extension can talk to an MCP server running on the user’s machine, what’s stopping it from accessing sensitive resources or executing privileged actions through the MCP?
MCP: Open by Default
Let’s first understand how MCP clients communicate with MCP servers. There are 2 standard transport implementations -
Server-Sent Events (SSE) — enables the MCP server to communicate through HTTP POST requests.
Standard Input/Output (stdio) — enables the MCP server to communicate through the process’s standard input and output streams.
When implementing an MCP server, the developer can choose how the MCP server will communicate. The server can support both transport methods.
It’s important to note that the transport layers themselves do not implement, or require, any authentication mechanism. It is up to the MCP server developer to implement access controls, but in practice, nearly all MCP servers today do not enforce authentication by default.
For local use, an MCP server that relies on Server-Sent Events (SSE) typically binds to a port on localhost, making it accessible from processes running on the same machine (like an MCP client).
Sandbox, Meet Sledgehammer
Now that we understand how a local SSE-based MCP server operates, and that it’s generally accessible to processes running on the same machine, we can revisit the question: can a Chrome extension access it as well?
The communication flow is fairly straightforward:
The client sends a GET request to the server to obtain a session ID and a messages endpoint — without any form of authentication.
Once initialized, the client can issue POST requests to that message’s endpoint to retrieve the list of available tools exposed by the MCP server and invoke them directly.
Client-Server communication illustration
First we set up a local SSE-based MCP server from
mcp.so
, specifically choosing a file-system variant, which allows AI clients to interact with the local file system. Following the setup instructions in the server’s README:
node dist/index.js ~/work/mcp/private_directory
Next we built a Chrome extension that runs in the background and attempts to connect to localhost:3001 - a commonly used port for local SSE-based MCP servers. Of course, this port may vary, so a real-world extension would need to scan local ports to locate the active MCP instance. The extension gets the server information, retrieves the tools list and tries to invoke the tools provided by the MCP server:
The Chrome extension had
unrestricted
access to the MCP server’s tools — no authentication needed — and was interacting with the file system as if it were a core part of the server’s exposed capabilities. The potential impact of this is massive, opening the door for malicious exploitation and complete system compromise.

data.title: Show HN: Hyperparam: OSS tools for exploring datasets locally in the browser
data.author: platypii
data.article_summary: Hyperparam是一家致力于解决机器学习中数据处理工具不足问题的公司，旨在提供一个用户友好、可扩展的界面，帮助数据科学家高效探索和处理大规模数据集。其核心目标是提升数据质量，因为数据质量对ML模型的成功至关重要。Hyperparam通过高效的数据格式、高性能JavaScript库以及AI辅助技术，使用户能够在浏览器中直接查看和处理TB级数据，而无需复杂的基础设施。其产品包括开源工具Hyparquet，一个纯JavaScript实现的Parquet文件读取库，支持在浏览器中无服务器访问大型数据集，具备高效流处理、压缩支持和轻量级特性。Hyperparam的愿景是通过数据质量的提升，促进更好模型的开发，同时确保隐私和合规性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于新工具的命名、功能、技术选择及实用性的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• **命名质疑**：abeppu认为工具的名称具有误导性，因为它与人们通常理解的超参数（hyperparameters）概念无关，且在工具描述中对超参数一词的使用也不准确。
• **积极评价**：pranshu54和yujian对工具表示了赞赏，认为其在网页上展示数据的功能很有趣。
• **技术选择比较**：
  ◦ wbradmoore质疑为什么选择当前技术实现而不是WASM，认为像duckdb-wasm或datafusion-wasm也能实现相同功能。
  ◦ barabbababoon也提到了duckdb-wasm，询问该工具是否是其轻量级版本。
• **实用性讨论**：
  ◦ klntsky指出工具名称过多而功能单一，并建议开发一个专注于数据迁移或处理管道的LLM聊天应用会更有益。
  ◦ newusertoday对工具在Parquet文件上的应用表示赞赏，并提到之前没有找到类似的工具。
• **安全性关注**：dmosites对iceberg读取器的认证处理能力提出了疑问，指出大多数iceberg表格并非公开访问。
• **隐私与性能**：
  ◦ doppenhe关心`npx hyperparam dataset.parquet`命令是否会向外部发送数据。
  ◦ cyrdax询问是否有人将该工具与duckdb-wasm进行了性能对比测试。

补充讨论：
• **语言偏好**：lorr1在回复中简短地表达了对Python语言的不满，但未直接针对工具本身，因此可以视为题外话。

争议焦点：
• 工具命名是否准确反映其功能，特别是与超参数概念的关系。
• 技术实现的选择是否最优，尤其是与WASM实现的比较。

43857856.article_content:
Hyperparam Open-Source
Hyperparam was founded to address a critical gap in the machine learning ecosystem: the lack of a user-friendly, scalable UI for exploring and curating massive datasets.
Our mission is grounded in the belief that data quality is the most important factor in ML success, and that better tools are needed to build better training sets. In practice, this means enabling data scientists and engineers to
“look at your data”
– even terabyte-scale text corpora – interactively and entirely in-browser without heavy infrastructure. By combining efficient data formats, high-performance JavaScript libraries, and emerging AI assistance, Hyperparam's vision is to put data quality front and center in model development. Our motto
“the missing UI for AI data”
reflects its goal to make massive data exploration, labeling, and quality management as intuitive as modern web apps, all while respecting privacy and compliance through a local-first design.
Mission and Vision: Data-Centric AI in the Browser
Our mission is to empower ML practitioners to create the best training datasets for the best models. This stems from an industry-wide realization that
model performance is ultimately bounded by data quality
, not just model architecture or hyperparameters. Hyperparam envisions a new workflow where:
Interactive Data Exploration at Scale:
Users can freely explore huge datasets (millions or billions of records) with fast, free-form interactions to uncover insights. Unlike traditional Python notebooks that struggle with large data (often requiring downsampling or clunky pagination), Hyperparam leverages browser technology for a smooth UI.
AI-Assisted Curation:
Hyperparam integrates ML models to help label, filter, and transform data at a scale that would be impractical to review manually. By combining a highly interactive UI with model assistance, we make it possible for the user to use data to express exactly what they want from the model.
Local-First and Private:
Hyperparam runs entirely client-side, with no server dependency. This design not only simplifies setup (no complex pipeline or cloud needed) but also addresses enterprise compliance and security concerns, since sensitive data need not leave the user's machine. Fully browser-contained tools can bypass major adoption hurdles.
Experts across data engineering and MLOps widely agree on the need for better data exploration and labeling tools to tackle today's bottlenecks. We believe that the way to do that is to make data-centric AI workflows that are faster, easier to deploy, and more scalable – enabling users to iteratively improve data quality, which in turn yields better models.
The Hyperparam OSS Universe
Hyperparam delivers on our vision through a suite of open-source tools that tackle different aspects of data curation. These tools are built in TypeScript/JavaScript for seamless browser and Node.js usage.
We care about performance, minimal dependencies, and standards compliance.
Hyparquet: In-Browser Parquet Data Access
Hyparquet
is a lightweight, pure-JS library for reading
Apache Parquet
files directly in the browser. Parquet is a popular columnar format for large datasets, and Hyparquet enables web applications to tap into that efficiency without any server.
Hyparquet allows data scientists to open large dataset files instantly in a browser UI for examination, without needing Python scripts, servers, or cloud databases. It's useful for quick dataset validation (e.g. checking a sample of a new data for quality issues) and for powering web-based data analysis tools. Because it's pure JS, developers can integrate Hyparquet into any web app or Electron application that needs to read Parquet. It is the core engine behind Hyperparam's own dataset viewer, enabling what was previously thought impossible:
client-side
big data exploration.
Browser-Native & Dependency-Free:
Hyparquet has
zero external dependencies
and is designed to run in both modern browsers and Node.js. At ~9.7 KB gzipped, it's extremely lightweight. It implements the full Parquet specification, aiming to be the “world's most compliant Parquet parser” that can open more files (all encodings and types) than other libraries.
Efficient Streaming of Massive Data:
Built with performance in mind, Hyparquet only loads the portions of data needed for a given query or view. It leverages Parquet's built-in indexing to fetch just the required rows or columns on the fly. This “load just in time” approach makes it feasible to interactively explore multi-gigabyte or even billion-row datasets in a web app.
Complete Compression Support:
Parquet files often use compression (Snappy, Gzip, ZSTD, etc.). Hyparquet by default handles common cases (uncompressed, Snappy), and with a companion library Hyparquet-Compressors, it supports
all
Parquet compression codecs. This is achieved with WebAssembly-optimized decompressors – notably HySnappy, a WASM Snappy decoder that accelerates parsing with minimal footprint.

data.title: When ChatGPT broke the field of NLP: An oral history
data.author: mathgenius
data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了自然语言处理（NLP）领域的巨大变革，特别是由于transformer模型和大型语言模型（LLM）的出现所引发的范式转变。2017年，Google研究人员提出了transformer模型，尽管最初并未被广泛认可，但其在NLP领域的潜力很快显现。2019年，BERT模型的推出标志着一个重要里程碑，随后LLM技术迅速普及，带来了科学发现、行业颠覆和广泛讨论。文章通过采访19位NLP研究人员，展示了这一技术变革对他们的影响，从最初的怀疑到逐渐接受，甚至有人经历了“存在危机”。这场变革不仅改变了NLP领域，也对整个AI社区产生了深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大语言模型（LLMs）对传统自然语言处理（NLP）的影响及未来发展

不同观点：
• teruakohatu：认为LLMs使许多历史研究变得过时，但传统NLP仍有其价值，特别是在成本和特定任务上。例如，VADER模型在情感分析中虽然有缺陷，但成本远低于LLMs。
• Al-Khwarizmi：承认LLMs对NLP领域的影响巨大，许多研究课题已被取代，但低层次任务如词性标注、句法解析和命名实体识别仍有一定应用，特别是在专业领域。尽管个人研究可能变得 irrelevant，但学术系统有其惯性，领域不会立即消亡。
• horsh1：主张传统NLP的正式表示方法仍有必要，特别是在工程和形式化任务中。LLMs在高效挖掘和分析正式表示方面仍有不足，传统NLP的任务（如法律语料的形式化）仍需依靠传统方法。
• whoaann_92：认为LLMs是NLP的一个新里程碑，特别是在数据标注和原型设计中非常有用。但在大规模高强度数据应用中，训练专用模型仍是必要且经济的。
• vjerancrnjak：指出在LLMs之前，低层次任务从未导致良好的总结或翻译系统，而transformers实现了这一飞跃，取消了对许多低层次任务的需求。
• AndrewKemendo：质疑“语言是唯一需要”的假设，认为智能可以通过非语言结构展示，LLMs的迭代过程是智能的基础。
• languagehacker：对AI和LLMs持保留态度，基于实际经验对模型的可靠性持怀疑态度，认为AI的过度炒作掩盖了NLP的实际挑战。
• cainxinth：关注商业利益对科学对话的影响，引用Tal Linzen的观点，指出某些对话者在公司中有巨大经济利益。
• thom：认为AI的炒作掩盖了NLP的实际进展，指出尽管工具更好，但核心挑战依旧存在，特别是在与AI初创公司对话时感受到的误解。
• mollerhoj：认为Google的BERT得到了过多赞誉，而真正的创新是ULMfit。
• gitroom：表达了对工作在一夜之间变得无意义的失落感，尽管对技术进步感到兴奋。
• softwaredoug：好奇LLMs对语言学，特别是普遍语法理论的影响。
• o11c：质疑是否有LLM能可靠地不忽略"not"这个词，认为这是相对于先前NLP的倒退。
• Animats：幽默地指出拥有 tenure 在这种变革时期是个优势。

补充讨论：
• LLMs对传统NLP的冲击：许多讨论者承认LLMs在许多NLP任务中的优势，但也指出传统方法在成本、特定应用和形式化任务中仍有价值。
• 学术与商业利益：关注商业利益对科学对话的影响，以及学术系统的惯性如何使某些领域在实际上已经过时但仍继续存在。
• 可靠性与实际应用：对LLMs的可靠性和实际应用中的局限性提出质疑，特别是与传统NLP方法相比。
• 低层次任务的持续应用：尽管LLMs在高级任务中表现出色，低层次的NLP任务（如词性标注和句法解析）在某些专业领域仍有其应用价值。

When ChatGPT Broke an Entire Field: An Oral History
By
John Pavlus
April 30, 2025
Researchers in “natural language processing” tried to tame human language. Then came the transformer.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
James O’Brien for
Quanta Magazine
Something very significant has happened to the field.
And also to people.
—Christopher Potts
By
John Pavlus
Contributing Writer
April 30, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
artificial intelligence
computer science
machine learning
natural language processing
neural networks
All topics
A
sking scientists to identify a paradigm shift, especially in real time, can be tricky. After all, truly ground-shifting updates in knowledge may take decades to unfold. But you don’t necessarily have to invoke the P-word to acknowledge that one field in particular —
natural language processing
, or NLP — has changed. A lot.
The goal of natural language processing is right there on the tin: making the unruliness of human language (the “natural” part) tractable by computers (the “processing” part). A blend of engineering and science that dates back to the 1940s, NLP gave Stephen Hawking a voice, Siri a brain and social media companies another way to target us with ads. It was also ground zero for the emergence of large language models — a technology that NLP helped to invent but whose explosive growth and transformative power still managed to take many people in the field entirely by surprise.
To put it another way: In 2019,
Quanta
reported on a then-groundbreaking
NLP system called BERT
without once using the phrase “large language model.” A mere five and a half years later, LLMs are everywhere, igniting discovery, disruption and debate in whatever scientific community they touch. But the one they touched first — for better, worse and everything in between — was natural language processing. What did that impact feel like to the people experiencing it firsthand?
Quanta
interviewed 19 current and former NLP researchers to tell that story. From experts to students, tenured academics to startup founders, they describe a series of moments — dawning realizations, elated encounters and at least one “existential crisis” — that changed their world. And ours.
* * *
Prologue: Before the Flood
transformers • BERTology • scale
By 2017,
neural networks
had already changed the status quo in NLP. But that summer, in a now-seminal paper titled “
Attention Is All You Need
,” researchers at Google introduced an entirely new kind of neural network called the transformer that would soon dominate the field. Not everyone saw it coming.
ELLIE PAVLICK
(assistant professor of computer science and linguistics, Brown University; research scientist, Google DeepMind)
:
Google had organized a workshop in New York for academics to hang out with their researchers, and Jakob Uszkoreit, one of the authors on that paper, was presenting on it. He was making a really clear point about how aggressively this model was not designed with any insights from language. Almost trolling a bit: I’m going to just talk about all these random decisions we made, look how absurd this is, but look how well it works.
There had already been a feeling of the neural nets taking over, and so people were very skeptical and pushing back. Everyone’s main takeaway was, “This is all just hacks.”
RAY MOONEY
(director, UT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, University of Texas at Austin)
:
It was sort of interesting, but it wasn’t an immediate breakthrough, right? It wasn’t like the next day the world changed. I really do think it’s not conceptually the right model for how to process language. I just didn’t realize that if you trained that very conceptually wrong model on a lot of data, it could do amazing things.
NAZNEEN RAJANI
(founder and CEO, Collinear AI; at the time a Ph.D. student studying with Ray Mooney)
:
I clearly remember reading “Attention Is All You Need” in our NLP reading group. Ray actually ran it, and we had this very lively discussion. The concept of
attention
had
been around for a while
, and maybe that’s why Ray’s reaction was kind of, “Meh.” But we were like, “Wow, this seems like a turning point.”
R. THOMAS MCCOY
(assistant professor, department of linguistics, Yale University)
:
During that summer, I vividly remember members of the research team I was on asking, “Should we look into these transformers?” and everyone concluding, “No, they’re clearly just a flash in the pan.”
Christopher Potts (chair, department of linguistics, Stanford University)

CHRISTOPHER POTTS
(chair, department of linguistics, Stanford Un

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了Owen Le Blanc及其创建的第一个Linux发行版MCC Interim Linux。1992年初，Le Blanc在曼彻斯特计算中心（MCC）工作时开发了这一发行版，旨在简化Linux的安装过程。当时，Linux内核虽已发布，但缺乏易用的安装工具，Le Blanc利用了Ted Ts'o的ramdisk代码和H. J. Lu的原型发行版，并编写了首个Linux fdisk工具。MCC Interim Linux通过两张软盘安装，显著提高了安装效率，被用于大学课程。虽然最初版本难以找到，但后续版本保存在ibiblio等档案中。该项目持续约七年，最后更新于1998年初。尽管未商业发行，但被包含在一些Linux工具包CD中。

Owen Le Blanc: creator of the first Linux distribution
By
Joe Brockmeier
April 21, 2025
Ask a Linux enthusiast who created the Linux kernel, and odds are they will have
no trouble naming Linus Torvalds—but many would be stumped if asked what the
first Linux distribution was, and who created it. Some might guess
Slackware
, or its predecessor,
Softlanding Linux
System
(SLS); both were arguably more influential but arrived just a bit
later. The first honest-to-goodness distribution with a proper installer was
MCC Interim Linux
,
created by Owen Le Blanc, released publicly in early 1992. I recently
reached out to Le Blanc to learn more about his work on the distribution, what
he has been doing since, and his thoughts on Linux in 2025.
When Torvalds first released the Linux kernel, he also provided "boot" and "root"
disk images (intended for
5¼-inch
floppy disks
) to help users
create a Linux system. There was not a proper installer, and users had to collect
several other utilities to pull together a working system. This was not, even for the
time,
particularly
user friendly
. Clearly, Linux was going to need a little extra help on its path
to world domination.
MCC Interim Linux
Le Blanc worked for the Manchester Computing Centre (MCC) at the
University of Manchester
from 1985
through 2016. He had been working with
CDC 7600
and
Cyber 170/730
machines, and
eventually began working with
HP 9000
workstations. Those ran
Hewlett Packard's Unix,
HP-UX
, which
made him want to learn more about Unix. He started with
Xenix
, but wanted something easier to
use. He said that he also tried
MINIX
, but it was difficult to get
working on a
Intel 80486 CPU
. When
Torvalds announced Linux, Le Blanc decided to give it a try, and that too was a
fair amount of work.
It was fairly hard to install Linux at first, because I think you
needed both MS-DOS and Minix -- we used a bootloader from Minix before
Werner Almesberger wrote LILO. You needed Minix because the DOS fdisk
program could not write partitions for other operating systems, and
you needed DOS if you wanted to do networking.
He was interested in improving the installation and created a Linux
system that could be installed from a pair of floppy disks. He made
use of ramdisk code by Ted Ts'o, took binaries from a
proto-distribution
created by H. J. Lu, and he wrote the original Linux fdisk
"
bugs and all
" for the project. According to the
MCC
README
for version 0.99.p10+, Le Blanc used his
distribution to install Linux on
386-SX
machines
for the university's C and Unix courses. It was possible to install
Linux on 12 machines in about an hour, according to the
documentation, certainly an improvement over earlier installation
methods. Eventually, he asked his department if he could share the
work that he had been doing.
The department was reluctantly willing, provided (1) I gave them some
credit for supporting its development, and (2) I made certain they had
no responsibility for ongoing support for users.  We agreed that
calling it "MCC Interim Linux" suggested that MCC had developed it,
and it was not intended to be a long term project.
The first MCC Interim Linux release (0.12) from February 1992, is,
if not completely lost, certainly hard to find online. The
1.0
release
is preserved on the ibiblio archive with other
historic
distributions
such as Yggdrasil, Red Hat's "Mother's Day" 1.0
release, and SLS 1.03 and 1.05.
The distribution
included things like
GCC
,
GNU Awk
,
GNU Emacs
, and the
info
packages because they were used in the university's courses. He did
not attempt to include a wide assortment of other software, such as
XFree86
(then X386), though.

Later releases can be found on
debian.mcc.ac.uk
,
in the
non-debian
directory. It has several releases, up to
the final
2.0
release
from 1996. I had asked Le Blanc whether MCC had
been distributed commercially, and he said no one had ever sold copies
of MCC that he was aware of though "
there were certainly people who
passed disks to others
". While doing some digging, though, I found
that
Walnut
Creek
had included MCC in some of its Linux Toolkit CD sets. For
example, the Internet Archive has the
March 1997
set with MCC Interim Linux 1.0+, along with Slackware, Debian,
MkLinux, and others. Readers who have older Linux Toolkit CD sets, or similar
sets, gathering dust in their closets may have even earlier versions.
In all, Le Blanc said that the
project ran about seven years, with the last updates to the
distribution being released in early 1998. Duri

data.article_summary: MIT神经科学家的一项新研究发现，多巴胺通过大脑特定区域间的神经回路，帮助小鼠在危险消失后消除恐惧。研究显示，多巴胺释放充当“解除警报”信号，使小鼠能够忘记与特定地点相关的恐惧。该机制涉及腹侧被盖区（VTA）向杏仁核不同区域发送多巴胺信号，激活与奖励相关的神经元，从而驱动恐惧的消退。具体而言，Rspo2基因表达的神经元负责编码恐惧记忆，而Ppp1r1b基因表达的神经元则编码恐惧消除记忆。多巴胺通过激活Ppp1r1b神经元，促进恐惧的消除，这一过程不仅仅是抑制恐惧，而是一种由大脑奖励机制驱动的积极学习过程。该研究为理解和治疗创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）等恐惧相关疾病提供了新思路。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多巴胺在恐惧消退和大脑功能中的作用及其复杂性

不同观点：
• Aurornis认为多巴胺只是信号分子，其在脑内不同区域的作用非常复杂，不能简单地将其视为可升降的“水平”。他强调多巴胺的作用远不止一两种功能，并提供了相关研究证明在不同脑区多巴胺信号的变化。
• ednite分享了个人经历，描述了一次恐惧转化为专注的体验，暗示多巴胺系统在压力下可能产生积极的学习效果。
• abhisek提出如何控制多巴胺以提高专注力，关注实际应用问题，如如何避免分心。
• justanotherjoe赞赏文章标题的启发性，认为它能够引发对多种经验的综合思考。
• voytec指出讨论中缺少对肾上腺素和去甲肾上腺素的提及，强调多巴胺只是更广泛化学反应的一部分，三者共同作用于压力反应系统。
• michaelbrave推测多巴胺与ADHD和焦虑之间的潜在联系，认为ADHD可能与多巴胺缺乏有关。
• castillar76对多巴胺处理困难导致神经发散大脑焦虑增加的可能性表示兴趣。
• mountainriver表达了对焦虑治疗进展的感激，并希望结合脑刺激技术进一步研究。
• Havoc提到极端运动中的“刺激时刻”涉及肾上腺素和多巴胺，认为这与恐惧消退有相似之处。
• carlgreene强调研究证明多巴胺在恐惧消退中的主动作用，并期待通过调节VTA→BLA通路或D1受体来改善PTSD和焦虑的治疗。
• childintime通过观察帕金森病患者，认为永久性恐惧反应可能与静态恐惧反应有关。
• seydor赞赏Tonegawa实验室在记忆研究中的先锋作用。
• elia_42对多巴胺在将新积极经验叠加到过去恐惧相关记忆中的作用表示好奇，并关注其在治疗中的潜在效果。
• pgt指出多巴胺重新平衡神经元权重，认为其改变恐惧和愿望是合理的。
• ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7用“大声噪音引发雪崩”来比喻多巴胺作用的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• 多巴胺作用的区域性和复杂性是讨论的核心，许多人指出不能简单化理解多巴胺的功能。
• 讨论中涉及多巴胺与焦虑、ADHD、帕金森病、极端运动和记忆处理的关系，显示其广泛的生物学和心理学影响。
• 对多巴胺调控的实际应用，如提高专注力和治疗焦虑，也被多次提及。
• 争议的焦点在于如何准确理解和应用多巴胺相关研究成果，特别是在治疗和实际生活中的应用。

43860726.article_content:
April 28, 2025
Research Findings
Dopamine signals when a fear can be forgotten
Study shows how a dopamine circuit between two brain regions enables mice to extinguish fear after a peril has passed.
Dangers come but dangers also go and when they do, the brain has an “all-clear” signal that teaches it to extinguish its fear. A new study in mice by MIT neuroscientists shows that the signal is the release of dopamine along a specific interregional brain circuit. The research therefore pinpoints a potentially critical mechanism of mental health, restoring calm when it works, but prolonging anxiety or even post-traumatic stress disorder when it doesn’t.
“Dopamine is essential to initiate fear extinction,” said Michele Pignatelli di Spinazzola, co-author of the new study from the lab of senior author
Susumu Tonegawa
, Picower Professor of biology and neuroscience at the RIKEN-MIT Laboratory for Neural Circuit Genetics in The Picower Institute for Learning and Memory and an HHMI Investigator.
In 2020
Tonegawa’s lab showed
that learning to be afraid, and then learning when that’s no longer necessary, result from a competition between populations of cells in the brain’s amygdala region. When a mouse learns that a place is “dangerous” (because it gets a little foot shock there), the fear memory is encoded by neurons in the anterior of the basolateral amygdala (aBLA) that express the gene Rspo2. When the mouse then learns that a place is no longer associated with danger (because they wait there and the zap doesn’t recur), neurons in the posterior basolateral amygdala (pBLA) that express the gene Ppp1r1b encode a new fear extinction memory that overcomes the original dread. Notably those same neurons encode feelings of reward, helping to explain why it feels so good when we realize that an expected danger has dwindled.
In the new study, the lab, led by former members Xiangyu Zhang and Katelyn Flick, sought to determine what prompts these amygdala neurons to encode these memories. The rigorous set of experiments the team reports in the
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
show that it’s dopamine sent to the different amygdala populations from distinct groups of neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA).
“Our study uncovers a precise mechanism by which dopamine helps the brain unlearn fear,” said Zhang, who also led the 2020 study and is now Senior Associate at Orbimed, a healthcare investment firm. “We found that dopamine activates specific amygdala neurons tied to reward, which in turn drive fear extinction. We now see that unlearning fear isn’t just about suppressing it—it’s a positive learning process powered by the brain’s reward machinery. This opens up new avenues for understanding and potentially treating fear-related disorders like PTSD.”
Forgetting fear
The VTA was the lab’s prime suspect to be the source of the signal because the region is well known for encoding surprising experiences and instructing the brain, with dopamine, to learn from them. The first set of experiments in the paper used multiple methods for tracing neural circuits to see whether and how cells in the VTA and the amygdala connect. They found a clear pattern: Rspo2 neurons were targeted by dopaminergic neurons in the anterior and left and right sides of the VTA. Ppp1r1b neurons received dopaminergic input from neurons in the center and posterior sections of the VTA. The density of connections was greater on the Ppp1r1b neurons than for the Rspo2 ones.
An edited version of a figure from the research shows the ventral tegmental area, highlighting dopamine-associated neurons in green and one that connects to the posterior amygdala (magnified in inset) in red.
The circuit tracing showed that dopamine is available to amygdala neurons that encode fear and its extinction, but do those neurons care about dopamine? The team showed that indeed they express “D1” receptors for the neuromodulator. Commensurate with the degree of dopamine connectivity, Ppp1r1b cells had more receptors than Rspo2 neurons.
Dopamine does a lot of things, so the next question was whether its activity in the amygdala actually correlated with fear encoding and extinction. Using a method to track and visualize it in the brain, the team watched dopamine in the amygdala as mice underwent a three-day experiment. On day one they went to an enclosure where they experienced three little zaps on the feet. On day two they went back to the enclosure for 45 minutes where they didn’t experience any new shocks –at first the mice froze in fear but then relaxed after about 15 minutes. On day 3 they returned again to test whether they had indeed extinguished the fear they showed at the beginning of day 2.
The dopamine activity tracking revealed that during the shocks on day 1, Rspo2 neurons had the larger response to dopamine, but in the early moments of day 2 when the anticipated shocks didn’t come and the mice eased up on freezing in fear, the Ppp1r1b neurons showed the stronger

data.title: Show HN: Roons – Mechanical Computer Kit
data.author: uncial
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为“roons”的机械计算机构建套件，灵感来源于机械逻辑门的视频。作者试图将机械逻辑门微型化，最终设计出一种“织布机自动机”，通过在交替的横杆上放置“roons”瓷砖来引导弹珠，实现比特流计算。该系统使用不同的roons实现各种逻辑门，如XOR和CANUTE，并通过弹珠的循环实现寄存器功能，达到图灵完备。文章还讨论了构建实用机械计算机套件的需求，包括紧凑性、快速处理、易于编辑和保存等特性。最终，作者成功制作了一个小型二进制加法器以及其他组件如内存和处理器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个复杂的机械装置引发的多方面讨论，包括命名建议、教育用途、技术细节、实际应用以及感官体验。

不同观点：
• **命名建议**：
  - [robbles] 认为装置中的"drive"可以改名为"clock drive"，因为该装置是由二进制时钟信号驱动的。
  
• **教育用途**：
  - [cuken] 强调该装置的物理实体性对帮助理解微观现象非常有帮助，类似于教育游戏"Spintronics"。
  - [jackpirate] 作为教授，表示希望将该装置放在办公室供学生使用，增强学习体验。
  - [duncancarroll] 认为该装置的可视化和触感非常适合用于教学。

• **技术比较与进化**：
  - [smoyer] 将该装置比作从"Turing Tumble"（类似于Duplos）进化到更高级的形式（类似于Legos）。
  - [novoreorx] 表示该装置复杂到难以理解，像是将虚拟游戏"shapez"搬到现实中。

• **实际应用与扩展**：
  - [sneha_tamal] 询问该装置是否仅用于教育和实验，还是可以扩展到更复杂的实际任务。
  - [Johnbot] 建议增加一个连续投放弹珠的漏斗装置，以增强实用性。

• **感官体验**：
  - [BlimpSpike] 关心装置的噪音问题，询问如果放在办公桌上是否会打扰到其他人。

• **幽默与文化参考**：
  - [shafoshaf] 提到装置与"Rockwell Turbo Encabulator"（一个技术幽默的虚构装置）的关联，增加讨论的趣味性。

补充讨论：
• **对项目的赞赏**：
  - 多位评论者（如[uticus], [sriram_malhar]）对项目的创意和执行表示高度赞赏。
  
• **技术细节的探讨**：
  - [uticus] 提出齿轮同步的技术细节，并引用维基百科上的"Key (engineering)"来解释。

争议焦点：
• 目前讨论中没有明显争议，主要为技术细节、命名建议和实际应用的多元看法。

Welcome, weary traveller from the orange site! Let me tell you the tale of
roons
— a kit for building mechanical computers.
I got inspired a couple of years ago when I binged a bunch of mechanical logic gate YouTube videos. There are some unbelievably clever implementations — Steve Mould’s
water computer
was a particular inspiration.
Still, these mechanical logic gates usually end up too big to make any practical devices. I figured, how hard can it be to miniaturise them into a usable kit?
foreshadowing
Very! It turned out the answer was
very hard
.
loom automaton
The Analytical Engine weaves algebraic patterns just as the Jacquard loom weaves flowers and leaves.
Ada Lovelace
After noodling around with far too many prototypes, I settled on what I call a
loom automaton
. We place tiles (“
roons
”) on a loom of alternating bars that move up and down. The contours on these tiles guide marbles
and holes
in discretised steps, representing bitstreams.
xor gate, composed of a turn + switch + distributor
Isn’t it
incredibly neat
that a literal physical loom turns out to be a great substrate for Lovelace’s metaphorical loom?
Anyway — you can think of this loom as a cellular automaton, where each cell is:
Occupied
or empty
Raised or lowered
Controlled by one of a finite set of
roons
If you know of prior work on this kind of system, please
get in touch
! I don’t claim the loom automaton is original; I just haven’t seen it elsewhere.
why loom good
Initially, I was making ad-hoc devices for each computer component — a gadget for number comparison, which worked
like this
; and a gadget for addition, which worked
like that
; etc.
The loom was a turning point. Instead of a loose collection of dissimilar gadgets that plug in together,
everything
is implemented on the loom. (Except peripherals, which we’ll get to later.) This gives us a
common interface
for stitching together whatever devices we need — memory, instruction sets, whatever. It makes it trivial to deliver power in synchronised discrete steps to every component.
I tried several variations on the loom: moving the marbles using alternating pins; continuously guiding the marbles using slides rippling in a wave; replacing gravity with magnetic potentials; etc. You can read more about these failed attempts in the hardware/prototypes deep dive.
Turing completeness
You can skip this section if it’s obvious that discretised marble movements are Turing complete, but then you’d miss out on the beautiful interactive simulator:
00/00
00/00
loading…
show hn xor
I learned JavaScript for this.
When the
xor
roon
above receives its inputs, a single
(

will block each other. So an
xor
implements XOR.
Other
roons
implement other logic gates. The
canute
performs a check then kicks an
back one step, which lets us implement carry-like functions on a marble bitstream. There are also
roons
like the
trap
that can permanently store a piece of state.
Though actually, you don’t need any stateful
roons
to store state — you can just cycle a stream of
round in a loop, bam, you’ve got a register:
7-bit static register
7-bit read/write register
We read from this register using a
switch
to divert the path of an infinite stream of
. Meanwhile, the register is constantly reading in from one of two data sources: itself, or an input stream, depending on a 3rd signal channel. While this channel is
, the data loops; when it’s
, it gets overwritten by the external input, letting us perform a write.
But I’m getting off track. Trivially, XOR gates are Turing complete; my job is done, that’s a computer, we can all go home. Thank you.
convenience
“But wait! Being Turing complete isn’t enough to not suck!”
That’s a good point. To actually make a
good
mechanical computer kit, we need a few other things:
Compactness
— build interesting devices in a small area, with very few pieces — no warehouse-sized processors!
Promptness
— reasonable processing rate; don’t have to wait for
BB 10
steps before a computation finishes
Fast editing
— minimal friction to changing a pattern and running it. “Hot reloading” so a pattern can be edited while running.
Saving and loading
— can save your work to compact storage, then bring it back later
Minimal
— build many complex systems from a small number of core parts
Basically I wanted a kit that’s actually practical and fun for building circuits.
did you make one?
… yes!
Here’s a binary adder made of a
long turn
,
canute
, and
distributor
— which together are not much bigger than a postage stamp. (Wave your hands and amortise away the space occupied by the disk drive itself, I/O plumbing etc etc)
Because space is at such a premium, instead of staggering multiple XORs and ANDs, we just bundle it all into a single unit — it’s small but slow.

data.title: Fivetran to acquire Census
data.author: njaremko
data.article_summary: Fivetran计划收购Census，以扩展其数据平台能力，从数据摄取和转换延伸至治理数据的可靠传输，帮助客户将数据驱动决策落实到运营工具中。Census的 reverse ETL 引擎以其可靠性、速度、处理 schema 变化的能力以及与现代数据技术的无缝集成而著称，符合Fivetran对简便性、自动化和信任的标准。此次收购不仅是产品整合，更是共享愿景和文化的统一，旨在为客户提供更大价值。客户将能够自动化地将可信数据从数据平台同步到Salesforce、Marketo等工具中，实现分析与行动的无缝衔接，将洞察转化为成果。以Canva为例，通过Fivetran和Census的结合，实现了实时个性化营销，提升了用户参与度并节省了工程时间。Census在性能、低延迟和数据治理方面的优势使其成为Fivetran的理想补充。

43860108.article_content:
At Fivetran, our mission has always been to make access to data as simple, secure, and reliable as electricity. We started by solving one of the hardest parts of the data journey: building and maintaining the pipelines that move raw data from source systems into the warehouse, with zero maintenance and complete trust in the output. Over the years, weâve expanded that vision â adding new sources, deployment models, destinations, and transformation capabilities.
Fivetranâs agreement to acquire Census marks a major step forward in that journey. Census will extend our platform beyond ingestion and transformation, so Fivetran customers will be ableÂ  to reliably move governed data to the applications where decisions get made.
Censusâs reverse ETL engine stands out not just for its reliability and speed, but for how seamlessly it handles schema changes and integrates with modern data technologies. Other tools in the market offer reverse ETL, but many require heavy setup or ongoing tuning to stay reliable at scale. I believe Census is the best reverse ETL tool in the market. Census stood out for how thoughtfully it handled performance, schema volatility, and governance â making it a natural fit for Fivetranâs standards of simplicity, automation, and trust.
Beyond shared product principles, Fivetran and Census share a deep-rooted history that dates back to the founding days of both companies. As each company has scaled, so has our partnershipâreflected in hundreds of joint customers and strong alignment across our executive teams. This agreement is about more than the integration of two products; it's the unification of a shared vision and culture, anchored in our commitment to delivering even greater value for our customers.
What this means for our customers
Customers will be able to sync modeled, trusted data delivered by Fivetran into their data platform into operational tools like Salesforce, Marketo, Zendesk, and HubSpot â all with automation and observability. This is key to closing the loop between analytics and action â transforming insights into outcomes in the systems that drive customer engagement, sales, and operations.
In a perfect world, Fivetran would have Reverse ETL and we could just log into one platform, we could do ETL and reverse ETL in one place. That would be our preference.
â VP of Advanced Analytics at a global insurance brand
Census carries forward Fivetranâs philosophy of ease and simplicity into the activation layer, while maintaining the governance, automation, and reliability our customers expect from Fivetran. Customers like Canva, one of our joint customers, deliver real-time customer 360 use casesâlike personalized marketing, churn prevention, and lifecycle engagementâwithout needing custom code or ongoing maintenance. With over 170 million monthly users and more than 200 terabytes of data in Snowflake, Canva needed a way to move quickly from insight to action. Fivetran helped them ingest and model their data; Census helped them activate itâpushing enriched segments into Braze to personalize customer experiences.
The results: a 33% increase in email open rates, 2.5% lift in platform engagement, over $200,000 saved annually in engineering time, and the ability to create new audiences in under five minutes. Together, we helped Canva turn data into results.
Reverse ETL, done right
Reverse ETL may sound simpleâmove data out of the warehouse and into a SaaS toolâbut it presents its own set of engineering challenges compared to ingestion pipelines.
Schema drift and API changes:
SaaS application schemas are constantly evolving, and APIs often change with little notice. Census built a specialized change detection algorithm to detect changes in the warehouse and sync only whatâs neededâreliably and incrementally.
Performance and
low latency
:
Census supports single second latency for streaming use cases with Live Syncs and near real-time syncs for all others - ensuring business applications are powered by the latest, most accurate data.
Weâve been waiting for this moment for years and itâs finally here. With Census Live Syncs, reverse ETL on real-time data is now a reality.
Customers can now activate their real-time insights on a zero latency data infrastructure
, without the complex engineering work needed to build it. It's hard to overstate how fast this new sync engine is.
â Nikhil Benesch, Co-Founder and CTO, Materialize
Governance and extensibility:
Census keeps data in the customerâs warehouse by default and processes it securely, with compliance support across SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, and more. It supports role-based access control, audit logs, and APIs, enabling interoperability with tooling across the data stack.
These problems are not trivial. Building a reverse ETL platform that can handle many destinations and complex enterprise requirements takes time and real product focus. Censusâs team approached it the same way we do at Fivetranâby

data.title: AI code review: Should the author be the reviewer?
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了使用AI编写代码后，是否也应由AI进行代码审查的问题。作者Daksh是Greptile的联合创始人，他们的产品使用AI审查pull request以发现人类可能忽略的错误和不良模式。作者通过分析用户提交PR的数据，发现某些用户提交的PR数量远多于其他人，且一个名为“devin-ai-integration[bot]”的AI bot提交的PR数量最多。

文章指出，传统上不希望代码作者自己审查，因为需要“新鲜的视角”。然而，LLM（大型语言模型）是无状态的，每次调用都是独立请求，因此让AI审查自己的代码也算是“新视角”。此外，AI工具在执行任务时的“脚手架”（工作流程）不同，使得代码生成和审查实质上是两个不同的过程，类似于两辆车使用相同引擎但车体不同。

文章还提到，AI提高了程序员的速度和效率，但可能降低代码质量，因为提示（prompt）并不完美，工程师容易低估这一点且未仔细审查AI生成的代码。AI生成的代码常包含人类不易察觉的错误，而AI在发现这些错误方面比人类更有效。

总结：尽管AI生成代码需要更严格的审查，但AI审查工具在发现错误方面优于人类，因此用AI审查AI生成的代码是可行且有效的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成代码的审查和责任归属问题

不同观点：
• [svieira] 认为工程师在审查AI生成的代码时，无法像审查自己编写的代码那样仔细，因为AI生成代码的速度超过了人类思考和输入的速度。同时， mediocre的工程师在使用AI后代码质量有所提高，AI使得好坏工程师的代码质量趋于一致。
• [gonzan] 认为AI工具正在改进，可以进行自我审查和预审查，但仍然需要人类审查AI生成的代码。他提到自己的工具Kamara在代码审查中发现了问题，即使是AI自己生成的代码。同时，他认为AI并没有达到100%准确，仍需要人类监督。
• [rbren] 强调了AI生成的PR如果没有明确的责任人，可能导致无人负责的问题。他的团队通过让PR与人类绑定，解决了这一问题，确保每个PR都有明确的负责人。
• [SOTGO] 关注AI在代码审查中产生误报的问题，认为AI有时会发现不存在的“bug”，因此对AI审查的结果需要谨慎对待。
• [simonw] 认为无论是否使用AI，程序员都应对自己提交的代码负责。AI只是辅助工具，最终责任仍在程序员身上，公司政策也应要求人类审查AI生成的代码。
• [taylodl] 提出了一种使用多个LLM和Cucumber构建自动化代码生成和审查管道的设想，认为这种方法在某些代码类型中可能有效，但需要人类审查Gherkin脚本和代码。
• [_heimdall] 坚持一个原则，即只批准自己愿意维护的代码，因此即使使用AI生成代码，也需要自己审查，不会完全依赖AI。
• [flimflamm] 建议将LLM的输出视为linter，第一轮审查可以依赖LLM，但仍需人类深入检查代码的正确性。
• [black3r] 认为AI生成的代码即使由同一个LLM审查，审查过程中的上下文是新的，因此不同于人类审查自己的代码。他主张至少需要一个人类审查AI生成的代码，尤其是对大型遗留代码库。
• [allisonee] 认为AI可以进行初步代码审查，但最终仍需人类审查代码，程序员应对自己提交的代码负全责。
• [pjmlp] 认为未来技术架构师的角色可能仅限于对交付物进行最终审查。
• [devrandoom] 强调自己审查自己的代码并不算真正的代码审查，因为人类容易看到自己想写的代码，而不是实际写出的代码，AI也是如此。
• [JonChesterfield] 认为让AI审查自己的代码是不可靠的，因为即使AI给出了答案，也可能是不正确的，类似于计算机错误提示的经历。
• [aussieguy1234] 分享了自己使用AI进行“预代码审查”的经验，认为AI可以捕捉明显的问题和bug，从而加快审查过程，节省时间。
• [logicchains] 认为AI可以生成大量单元测试，并自动运行以验证代码行为，这有助于提高审查效率。即使AI写的测试可能依赖于实现细节，也可以在审查完成后丢弃。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI是否可以有效地审查自己生成的代码。一部分人认为AI审查缺乏“新鲜视角”，容易忽略问题，而另一部分人认为AI可以进行初步审查，但最终仍需人类审查。
• 责任归属问题是另一个讨论重点，即即使AI生成了代码，程序员仍应对代码质量负全责。
• AI在代码审查中的实际应用效果和误报问题也被多次提及，尤其是AI审查结果的可靠性。
• 一些人提出使用AI构建自动化代码生成和审查管道的设想，但普遍认为仍需人类监督和审查。

43857643.article_content:
Alternate title: I’m using AI to write code. Is it silly to use AI to review it?
I'm Daksh, a co-founder of Greptile. Our product uses AI to review pull requests to surface bugs and anti-patterns that humans might miss.
Here is an example
of what that looks like.
Recently, I was curious to see if there exists a power law in the number of PRs opened by individual Greptile users. In other words - were some users opening orders of magnitude more PRs than others? A quick SQL query later, I discovered that there is a power law to this.
I also noticed something else very interesting:
At the far left of the long list of GitHub usernames was “devin-ai-integration[bot]”.
An AI bot was writing more pull requests than any individual human. [1]
Seeing as Devin uses the same LLMs under-the-hood as Greptile, it does raise an interesting question - should the author be the reviewer?
[1] Granted that this is somewhat of a technicality. Devin’s contributions across many orgs are being counted in aggregate here. It would be more accurate to treat “Devin @ Company A” and “Devin @ Company B” as separate entries in this chart.
Should the Author Be The Reviewer?
Most software companies wouldn’t want the PR reviewer to be the same person as the PR author. A large part of why PR reviews happen is to ensure every new piece of code is getting a
fresh
set of eyes. It seems silly to have
Claude
Sonnet generate a bunch of code, and then expect Claude Sonnet to find bugs in it.
There are a few counterpoints worth discussing:
Statelessness
If you’ve used LLM APIs, you’ll notice that they are stateless. Every inference call is a clean slate request for intelligence. As a result - asking an LLM to review its own code
is
looking at it with a fresh set of eyes.
Scaffolding
Scaffolding refers generally to the specific workflows that a tool uses to wrap the LLM call to allow it to do the task at hand. For an AI code reviewer it might be the set of steps it takes to review a diff, checking for bugs, formulating comments, and finally self-assessing comment severity, plus the context retrieval along the way to ensure it’s looking at the relevant docs files and other code files in the codebase. For Devin, it likely is just as complex and completely different. In other words, the reviewer is in fact materially different from the author. These are two distinct cars that just happen to have the same
engine
.
How different are two humans, really?
In a pre-AI world, the author and reviewer of a PR are two distinct people. However, they contain the same intelligence at their core, not unlike two AI tools. Not only do they share a functionally identical brain from a biological standpoint, they even have shared knowledge since they are both trained engineers and shared context since they are coworkers at the same company.
AI-Generated Code Needs Closer Reviewing
AI code isn’t slop, but it is a little sloppy
There is no doubt that AI has made programmers faster and more effective. That said, in my opinion, AI has
reduced
the average quality of the code that
good
engineers write. This is not strictly because the models produce worse code than good engineers. It’s because:
Prompting is an imperfect and lossy way to communicate requirements to AI
Engineers underestimate the degree to which this is true, and don’t carefully review AI-generated code to the degree to which they would review their own.
The reason for #2 isn’t complacency, one can review code at the speed at which they can think and type, but not at the speed at which an LLM can generate.When you’re typing code, you review-as-you-go, when you AI-generate the code, you don’t.
Interestingly, the inverse is true for mediocre engineers, for whom AI actually improves the quality of the code they produce. AI simply makes good and bad engineers converge on the same median as they rely on it more heavily.
Humans are bad at catching the types of bugs that AI introduces
AI-generated code generally contains more bugs. Moreover, these bugs are not the type humans would introduce. How often have you found a
Cursor
’s “Apply” function changed a line of code you didn’t expect it would change, and you didn’t notice until later? How many of those bugs were things you could see yourself introducing without AI?
Moreover, PR review is not a great way to catch bugs.
Humans just aren’t that good at detecting them,
so PR review tends to be more of a style/pattern enforcement exercise, and on occasion an architecture review.
Oddly, it turns out AI
is
actually much better than humans at finding bugs in code. During our tests, we found the newest
Anthropic
Sonnet model correctly identified 32 out of the 209 bugs in the “hard” category of our bug finding benchmark. For reference, none of the highly skilled engineers at Greptile could identify more than 5-7.
Note that 32/209 isn’t
great
either, it’s just better than the human developer.

总结：尽管AI生成代码需要更严格的审查，但AI审查工具在发现错误方面优于人类，因此用AI审查AI生成的代码是可行且有效的。

data.title: Mac app launches slowed by malware scan (2024)
data.author: username223
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Mac应用程序启动缓慢的原因，主要聚焦于由`syspolicyd`进程中的`dispatchQueue "com.apple.security.syspolicy.yara"`引发的恶意软件扫描。作者通过`spindump`分析发现，`syspolicyd`在使用`yr_rules_scan_file`函数进行Yara规则扫描，导致应用启动延迟。然而，博主Howard Oakley对此提出异议，认为Yara规则扫描不太可能发生，并提出慢启动可能是由于计算SHA-256哈希以验证框架文件的信任所致。作者反驳Oakley的理论，认为其缺乏实证，并坚持自己的发现，即`spindump`显示了明显的恶意软件扫描调用链，如`perform_malware_scan_if_necessary`函数。作者强调，日志未必记录所有系统活动，而`spindump`提供了更直接的证据。Oakley则依赖日志消息，并推测存在未记录的哈希缓存，但作者认为这并不合理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mac系统中应用启动缓慢的问题及其原因，特别是涉及恶意软件扫描和代码验证的过程。

不同观点：
• john-h-k认为在macOS上运行个人项目编译器时，生成大量可执行文件的测试过程非常缓慢。相比之下，Linux Docker容器中的测试速度要快得多。即使通过一些变通方法，macOS上的速度仍然不如Linux。
• musicale提到这是syspolicyd引发的问题，暗示系统策略守护进程可能是导致速度慢的原因。
• davb分享了在指定iTerm2为"开发者工具"后，仍会在某些情况下进行公证检查的问题，比如在使用tmux时。不过，在更新到Sequoia (15.4.1)后，该问题不再出现。
• krackers假设Mac有一个缓存机制用于存储已启动应用的SHA-256哈希值，以加速后续启动。并引用了Apple的文档解释代码签名验证的流程，提出验证可能是按需进行的。
• eviks质疑内置系统库是否会被扫描以查找恶意软件，并建议用户应用也可以采用类似的只读机制以提高效率。
• larrywright怀疑Fusion 360启动缓慢可能与这个问题有关，尽管在相对现代的M1 MacBook Pro上运行。
• carlosjobim提供了一个解决Affinity Photo启动缓慢的简单方法，即复制应用文件并删除原始文件，从而显著提高启动速度。
• m3047提到MacOS自带YARA工具，暗示可能用于恶意软件扫描。
• lapcat作为作者，解释了该帖子的背景，并指出之前提交到HN时未获得关注。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到系统策略、缓存机制和代码验证对应用启动速度的影响。
• 提供了具体的变通方法和代码示例（如davb提供的测试脚本链接）。
• 争议的焦点在于macOS的恶意软件扫描和代码验证机制是否过度影响了应用的启动性能，特别是在开发者或高级用户的特定用例中。
• 不同的系统版本和硬件配置可能导致用户遇到的问题和解决方案有所不同。

43858970.article_content:
Why some Mac apps launch slowly: A follow-up
May 1 2025
Last year I wrote a blog post
Mac app launches slowed by malware scan
:
I discovered that the slow launches are caused by the
syspolicyd
process, specifically
DispatchQueue "com.apple.security.syspolicy.yara"
. The backtrace showed
syspolicyd
calling the
yr_rules_scan_file
function.
Recently, however, voluminous blogger Howard Oakley has written a series of blog posts, starting with
Why some apps launch very slowly
and culminating with
Why some apps sometimes launch extremely slowly
, that appear to be in denial of my discovery. Oakley says,
Malware scan using any known Yara rules is most unlikely, as:
XProtect Yara rules commonly include file size limits, resulting in few rules applying to larger files, and more rapid completion.
Known checks using Yara rules are all well-recorded in log entries, and the source of those rules is stated clearly.
Yara scans are normally reported with their result.
Scan results are succinct and hardly likely to be lost in a âcache missâ.
I'm truly baffled by this denial, because the backtrace I mentioned comes directly from spindumps (
/usr/sbin/spindump
), which take frequent (10 milliseconds by default) samples of all running processes on the system. Spindumps don't lie!
The spindumps also indicate that the
syspolicyd
malware checks are triggered by the
dlopen
function to load a dynamic library. These are the framework checks that Oakley mentions; a framework is essentially bundled dynamic library. You can see the series of function calls in the samples of the launching app:
dyld4::APIs::dlopen_from(
char const*, int, void*)
AppleSystemPolicy::fileCheckLibraryValidation(
proc*, fileglob*, long long, long long, unsigned long)
AppleSystemPolicy::perform_malware_scan_if_necessary(
ASPProcessInfo*, ASPEvaluationInfo*, int, ScanMeta*, int*, unsigned int, int, long long*)
AppleSystemPolicy::waitForEvaluation(
syspolicyd_evaluation*, int, ASPEvaluationInfo*, vnode**, evaluation_results*, long long*, char const*)
It doesn't get any more obvious than
perform_malware_scan_if_necessary
! And the app is literally waiting for the
syspolicyd
evaluation, hence the slow launch.
I tried to explain this to Oakley in the comments of one of his blog posts, but for some strange reason, he refuses to accept my points. In fact, he refuses to take or to read a spindump. At first he claimed it was too difficult for anyone except an "expert" like me, but I simply selected "Spindump" from the action menu in Activity Monitor and then did a text search of the resulting file. (On the other hand, you can control the timing of the spindump more precisely using the
spindump
command-line tool, even specifying that it should wait for a particular app to launch.)
Oakley's position appears to be that the log messages tell him everything that he needs to know, as if a phenomenon doesn't exist unless it's logged. As a computer programmer himself, Oakley ought to know better, because a log message occurs only if the programmer specifically, intentionally writes a logging statement in the program. Not everything that happens on your Mac is magically logged.
Here's Oakley's own theory about the slow launches:
The most likely activity to account for these long checking times is computation of SHA-256 hashes for the contents of each item in the appâs Frameworks folder. Thus, these occasional extremely long launch times are most probably due to time taken âevaluating trustâ by computing hashes for protected code in the Frameworks folder in the app bundle, when those hashes have been flushed from their cache.
Oakley seems to be claiming, with no empirical evidence, that Macs have a cache of SHA-256 hashes of all bundled files of all apps that have been launched. But where exactly is this cache??? I've never seen it or heard of such a thing. As far as I can tell, it's pure speculation by Oakley based on nothing but a terse log message:
com.apple.syspolicy.exec Recording cache miss for <private>
Ironically, the references to
com.apple.syspolicy.exec
and
AppleSystemPolicy
in his log messages appear to match quite well with the results of my spindumps. I don't deny that
something
is cached, but I think the evidence suggests that what is cached is the result of a malware scan, which for practical purposes would make a lot more sense than a bunch of hashes. After all, malware definitions are periodically updated for newly discovered malware, which means that the results of previous malware scans would eventually become outdated. Whereas Oakley's theory doesn't make much sense to me. The code signature of executables is
always
checked when the executable is loaded at runtime, so if the app has been modified since the previous launch, that would be detected anyway. Moreover, apps have some protections against modification: App Store apps are owned by the root user, and the App Management feature prevents (or is
supposed to prevent
) notarized apps from unauthori

data.title: Show HN: Robot Unlock – an open-ended programming game/zachlike
data.author: adrianton3
data.article_summary: 《Robot Unlock》是一款由Adrian Toncean开发和发布的开放式解谜游戏，计划于2025年5月1日发布。游戏包含75个以上的关卡，玩家需在有限空间内使用少量指令解决 puzzles，并可以优化解决方案在速度、指令或空间方面的表现。游戏支持多线程操作、设置断点以及逐步调试，并允许玩家创建和分享自定义关卡，同时解决其他社区玩家设计的关卡。玩家还可以比较各自解决方案的排名。系统要求包括64位处理器和操作系统，推荐使用Windows 11及至少4GB内存。目前无用户评价。游戏在发行首周提供9折优惠，价格为8.99美元。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一款游戏的兴趣及相关技术细节的讨论

不同观点：
• zellyn对游戏在Mac OS上的运行情况表示关注，特别是操作系统仅标注为"11"是否能兼容Mac。
• pimlottc指出对不熟悉该类型的用户来说，解释"zachlike"（类似Zachtronics风格的游戏）可能会有帮助。
• beardedmoose作为Zachtronics游戏的粉丝，表示会在下班后尝试，并询问了开发所用的编程语言或引擎。
• pwillia7对"zachlike"这一术语表示喜爱，显示出对该类型游戏的认同和幽默感。

补充讨论：
• citizenpaul认为如果游戏能添加用户自选的编程语言而不是通用符号会更有吸引力，并提到这类似于Scratch编程语言，强调了游戏的教育价值。

争议焦点：目前没有明显争议，但citizenpaul的评论隐含了对游戏通用性与教育性之间的取舍讨论。

data.title: LLMs for Engineering: Teaching Models to Design High Powered Rockets
data.author: tamassimond
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了大型语言模型（LLMs）在高端火箭设计中的应用。通过RocketBench基准测试，作者评估了LLMs在两个复杂设计任务中的表现：目标高度优化和精确着陆挑战。结果显示，尽管LLMs具备较强的基础工程知识，但在利用模拟结果进行设计迭代时表现不足。然而，结合强化学习（RL）后，一个70亿参数的模型在性能上超过了现有顶尖基础模型和人类专家。研究表明，经过RL训练的LLMs可以成为复杂工程优化的有效工具， potentially transforming engineering domains beyond software development.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）在工程领域的应用及局限性

不同观点：
• Workaccount2认为，LLMs在软件工程中表现较好，因为代码的结构化特点与LLMs的标记化处理方式非常契合。然而，机械制图和电子原理图等视觉语言更复杂，目前的LLMs难以有效处理这些内容。即便有一些工具如O3能够理解基础的电子原理图，但距离实际应用仍有很大差距。此外，训练数据量的不足也限制了LLMs在这方面的表现。

• Frumiousirc指出，基于机器学习的模型本质上是对现实的模拟，而这些模拟往往是不完美的。由于现实世界的复杂性，模型只能根据所提供的数据进行学习，因此在处理现实问题时可能会出现错误。例如，如果模拟中没有考虑横风的影响，模型就无法设计出应对横风的方案。这种局限性使得LLMs在科学和工程领域中的应用存在根本性缺陷，除非模型能够直接从现实中学习并调整。

• FilosofumRex认为，传统工程公司将LLMs整合到现有的模拟软件中是适得其反的。他主张由创新型公司从基础开始训练LLMs，并在需要特定数据时调用模拟软件。这种方法可以更好地利用LLMs的潜力，而不是简单地将它们嵌入现有的工作流程中。

• Simianwords提出，需要针对特定领域进行微调的模型，例如医学领域。他认为，通过使用大量的医学数据进行训练，可以开发出更有效的领域特定模型。

• Akomtu用比喻的方式说明了一个只掌握工程术语但缺乏实际工程知识的“假工程师”在面对实际设计任务时的荒谬表现。这反映了过度依赖LLMs可能导致的现实问题，即模型可能表面上看起来很专业，但实际上缺乏真正的理解和能力。

• Rel_ic对LLMs在工程领域的应用持怀疑态度，认为潜在的负面影响可能多于正面影响。

• Revskill提到LLMs在处理如停机问题等复杂逻辑问题时可能会陷入无限递归，这表明LLMs在处理某些计算理论问题时存在局限性。

• Aaron695提出了一种将LLMs视为“神”的集体信仰模式。他认为人们可以围绕LLMs形成一种集体智慧，通过不断的反馈和微调来改进模型。这种模式类似于某些宗教团体，通过共同信仰和合作来实现目标。

补充讨论：
• 讨论的焦点在于LLMs在工程和科学领域的应用潜力及局限性。争议的焦点包括模型对现实世界的模拟能力、领域特定模型的需求以及过度依赖LLMs可能导致的问题。

• 不同观点反映了LLMs在实际应用中面临的多方面挑战，包括技术上的局限性、数据量的限制以及人类对模型过度依赖可能带来的风险。

• 讨论还涉及到LLMs在特定领域（如医学和工程）的微调需求，以及通过集体合作和信仰模式来改进LLMs的潜在方法。

Title:
LLMs for Engineering: Teaching Models to Design High Powered Rockets
Authors:
Toby Simonds
View a PDF of the paper titled LLMs for Engineering: Teaching Models to Design High Powered Rockets, by Toby Simonds
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed software engineering, but their application to physical engineering domains remains underexplored. This paper evaluates LLMs' capabilities in high-powered rocketry design through RocketBench, a benchmark connecting LLMs to high-fidelity rocket simulations. We test models on two increasingly complex design tasks: target altitude optimization and precision landing challenges. Our findings reveal that while state-of-the-art LLMs demonstrate strong baseline engineering knowledge, they struggle to iterate on their designs when given simulation results and ultimately plateau below human performance levels. However, when enhanced with reinforcement learning (RL), we show that a 7B parameter model outperforms both SoTA foundation models and human experts. This research demonstrates that RL-trained LLMs can serve as effective tools for complex engineering optimization, potentially transforming engineering domains beyond software development.

data.title: Anubis saved our websites from a DDoS attack
data.author: DoctorOW
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在ScummVM项目中经历的一次DDoS攻击事件。起初，作者收到服务器负载增加的监控通知，但未发现明显异常。几天后，网站因服务器过载而崩溃，Apache、PHP-FPM和MariaDB均达到饱和。通过检查日志，作者发现大量来自同一IP的可疑请求，试图通过频繁访问特定页面来压垮服务器。最终，作者通过封锁该IP并优化服务器配置成功抵御攻击，网站恢复正常运行。此次事件被戏称为“阿努比斯拯救了我们的网站”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Anubis及其在防止DDoS攻击和AI爬虫方面的有效性与使用讨论

不同观点：
• **mrweasel**：不确定当前的攻击是DDoS还是AI爬虫引发的问题，认为现代AI公司不像传统搜索引擎那样尊重互联网基础设施，隐匿行为更明显，导致难以区分恶意攻击和爬虫行为。
• **CaptainFever**：认为Anubis只是DDoS保护工具的更新版，本质上与已有工具（如CloudFlare等）类似，质疑为何Anubis受到特别关注，可能只是因为营销得当。
• **chrisnight**：指出Anubis的验证机制对使用临时容器插件的用户不友好，每次关闭标签页后都需要重新生成token，尽管理解隐私保护的需求，但体验不佳。
• **butz**：提出Anubis部署后可能带来一些意外问题，例如影响正常文件下载或导致链接失效，强调需要仔细检查其对系统的影响。
• **vachina**：认为任何简单的验证机制（如Captcha或按钮点击）都能有效阻止大多数爬虫，不必依赖Anubis。
• **forty**：建议将PoW（工作量证明）系统集成到HTTP或TLS协议中，以避免对JS的依赖。
• **kh_hk**：指出当前的客户端PoW可能不足以长期应对，爬虫可以通过解决挑战并重用cookie绕过限制，提出使用JA4指纹识别作为额外验证手段。
• **Tiberium**：质疑Anubis对“诚实”标识用户代理的惩罚机制，认为这可能会促使爬虫伪装身份，奖励那些不道德的爬虫行为。
• **justusthane**：不理解Anubis如何解决特定DDoS问题，尤其是当攻击来自僵尸网络时，为何这些机器不花额外时间解决PoW。

补充讨论：
• **qiu3344**：支持Anubis，认为其抗爬虫机制比传统WAF/抗爬虫大厂更有效，且不依赖浏览器特性，避免了浏览器垄断文化的支持问题。
• **pmlnr**：询问是否有不依赖JS的解决方案。
• **gitroom**：提到Anubis涉及到开源社区中的法律规则和个人需求的平衡问题。
• **8474_s**：偏好Anubis的验证方式，认为比Cloudflare的验证更友好。

争议焦点：
• Anubis是否因为营销得当而受到过度关注，其实质是否与其他DDoS保护工具并无显著区别。
• Anubis对“诚实”标识用户代理的惩罚是否会适得其反，导致更不道德的爬虫行为。
• Anubis部署后对系统正常功能的可能影响及如何权衡其副作用。

总结：讨论围绕Anubis的实际效果、其对用户和系统的影响以及是否应该使用不依赖JS的解决方案展开，反映了技术社区对网络安全工具的复杂需求与权衡。

43864108.article_content:
The Day Anubis Saved Our Websites From a DDoS Attack
2025-05-01 14:00:00
#bts
#sysops
#webdev
One part of my work for the ScummVM project is helping to keep the server infrastructure up and running, including our primary server, which hosts our website, wiki, forums, and some internal applications.
About three weeks ago, I started receiving monitoring notifications indicating an increased load on the MariaDB server. This in itself is nothing too unusual. It usually means nothing but a sudden influx of new visitors, and in most cases, it is just a link being shared somewhere or a single IP trying to annoy us.
The notifications popped up and disappeared as quickly as they appeared. I started to look into the log files of our web server, and I didn’t notice anything too unusual, maybe a bit more background noise. This went on for a couple of days without seriously impacting our server or accessibility–it was a tad slower than usual.
And then the website went down.
We use a stack consisting of Apache2, PHP-FPM, and MariaDB to host the web applications. The server logs revealed that everything was saturated. Apache2 refused to accept new connections, the PHP-FPM pools were completely filled, and MariaDB also had no connections left.
Now, it was time to find out what was going on. Hoping that it was just one single IP trying to annoy us, I opened the access log of the day and was greeted by this:

43864108.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在ScummVM项目中经历的一次DDoS攻击事件。起初，作者收到服务器负载增加的监控通知，但未发现明显异常。几天后，网站因服务器过载而崩溃，Apache、PHP-FPM和MariaDB均达到饱和。通过检查日志，作者发现大量来自同一IP的可疑请求，试图通过频繁访问特定页面来压垮服务器。最终，作者通过封锁该IP并优化服务器配置成功抵御攻击，网站恢复正常运行。此次事件被戏称为“阿努比斯拯救了我们的网站”。

data.title: Show HN: Kubetail – Real-time log search for Kubernetes
data.author: andres
data.article_summary: Kubetail 是一个用于 Kubernetes 的实时日志展示工具，支持浏览器和终端查看。它可以从多容器工作负载中实时获取日志，并按时间线合并展示。Kubetail 通过 Kubernetes API 直接从集群中获取日志，无需外部服务。它支持按工作负载、时间范围和节点属性等过滤日志，并可在多个集群间切换。用户可以通过 Homebrew、Shell 脚本或二进制文件在桌面安装，也可使用 Helm 或 YAML 清单在集群中部署。Kubetail 提供了一个简洁易用的界面，方便开发者实时监控和分析 Kubernetes 日志。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kubernetes日志查看工具的比较与需求

不同观点：
• **支持GUI的日志查看工具**：corytheboyd认为理想的日志查看工具应具有图形用户界面（GUI），并能够深度集成结构化日志，提供强大的过滤功能。他提到希望有一个类似DataDog的本地化工具，而Grafana/Loki等工具过于繁重。

• **偏好命令行工具**：glitchcrab和nodesocket更喜欢使用命令行工具，如Stern和Kubetail。他们认为这些工具易于设置和使用，并且不需要web UI。nodesocket特别提到Kubetail的配置非常简单，比Loki+Grafana或ELK更易用。

• **本地化与隐私保护**：carlgreene强调了本地运行和不发送敏感日志到外部站点的重要性。他对合并多容器日志进行实时查看的功能表示赞赏，认为这是调试多pod工作负载的变革性功能。

• **对搜索功能的质疑**：otterley对该工具的搜索功能持怀疑态度，认为它更像是过滤而不是真正的搜索，与OpenSearch或Splunk不在同一水平。

• **缓存与存储问题**：ai-christianson询问日志是否被缓存或存储，或者完全依赖Kubernetes自身处理。

• **其他平台的需求**：nomilk提到自己不使用Kubernetes，但也在寻找类似的Heroku日志查看工具，尤其是本地搜索已归档日志的功能。

• **工具推荐**：Dlemo推荐了argocd，认为它也能显示容器日志，并再次提到了Grafana与Loki的组合。

• **工具间的比较**：badmonster直接询问该工具与Loki/Grafana或Stern的比较情况。

补充讨论：
• **工具的命名混淆**：hnlub提醒不要将此工具与另一个同名的Kubetail混淆，提供了相关GitHub链接以供区分。

• **对合并日志功能的赞赏**：gitroom表示合并所有pod日志的功能是他一直想要的，对此工具的实现表示赞赏。

整体来看，讨论的焦点集中在Kubernetes日志查看工具的界面类型（GUI vs 命令行）、功能（搜索与过滤）、易用性（设置与配置的简便性）以及与隐私保护相关的日志存储方式。不同用户根据自己的使用场景和偏好提出了各自的看法和需求。

Kubetail
Kubetail is a real-time logging dashboard for Kubernetes (browser/terminal)
Demo:
https://www.kubetail.com/demo
Introduction
Kubetail
is a general-purpose logging dashboard for Kubernetes, optimized for tailing logs across across multi-container workloads in real-time. With Kubetail, you can view logs from all the containers in a workload (e.g. Deployment or DaemonSet) merged into a single, chronological timeline, delivered to your browser or terminal.
The primary entry point for Kubetail is the
kubetail
CLI tool, which can launch a local web dashboard on your desktop or stream raw logs directly to your terminal. Behind the scenes, Kubetail uses your cluster's Kubernetes API to fetch logs directly from your cluster, so it works out of the box without needing to forward your logs to an external service first. Kubetail also uses your Kubernetes API to track container lifecycle events in order to keep your log timeline in sync as containers start, stop or get replaced. This makes it easy to follow logs seamlessly as user requests move from one ephemeral container to another across services.
Our goal is to build the most powerful, user-friendly logging platform for Kubernetes and we'd love your input. If you notice a bug or have a suggestion please create a GitHub Issue or send us an email (
hello@kubetail.com
)!
Features
Clean, easy-to-use interface
View log messages in real-time
Filter logs by:
Workload (e.g. Deployment, CronJob, StatefulSet)
Absolute or relative time range
Node properties (e.g. availability zone, CPU architecture, node ID)
Grep
Uses your Kubernetes API to retrieve log messages so data never leaves your possession (private by default)
Web dashboard can be installed on desktop or in cluster
Switch between multiple clusters (Desktop-only)
Quickstart (Desktop)
Option 1: Homebrew
First, install the Kubetail CLI tool (
kubetail
) via
homebrew
:
brew install kubetail
Next, start the web dashboard using the
serve
subcommand:
kubetail serve
This command will open
http://localhost:7500/
in your default browser. Have fun viewing your Kubernetes logs in realtime!
Option 2: Shell
First, download and run the install script:
curl -sS https://www.kubetail.com/install.sh | bash
Next, start the web dashboard using the
serve
subcommand:
kubetail serve
This command will open
http://localhost:7500/
in your default browser.
Option 3: Binaries
Download the binary for your OS/Arch (from the latest
release binaries
):
Darwin/amd64
Darwin/arm64
Linux/amd64
Linux/arm64
Windows/amd64
Rename the file and make it executable:
mv <filename> kubetail
chmod a+x kubetail
Next, start the web dashboard using the
serve
subcommand:
kubetail serve
This command will open
http://localhost:7500/
in your default browser.
Quickstart (Cluster)
Option 1: Helm
First, add the Kubetail org's chart repository, then install the "kubetail" chart:
helm repo add kubetail https://kubetail-org.github.io/helm-charts/
helm install kubetail kubetail/kubetail --namespace kubetail-system --create-namespace
For more information on how to configure the helm chart, see the chart's
values.yaml
file.
To access the web dashboard you can expose it as an ingress using the chart or you can use your usual access methods such as
kubectl port-forward
:
kubectl port-forward -n kubetail-system svc/kubetail-dashboard 8080:8080
Visit
http://localhost:8080
. Have fun viewing your Kubernetes logs in realtime!
Option 2: YAML Manifest
First, create a namespace for the Kubetail resources:
kubectl create namespace kubetail-system
Next, choose your authentication mode (
cluster
or
token
) and apply the latest manifest file:
#
For cluster-based authentication use kubetail-clusterauth.yaml:
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubetail-org/helm-charts/releases/latest/download/kubetail-clusterauth.yaml
#
For token-based authentication use kubetail-tokenauth.yaml:
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubetail-org/helm-charts/releases/latest/download/kubetail-tokenauth.yaml
To access the web dashboard you can use your usual access methods such as
kubectl port-forward
:
kubectl port-forward -n kubetail-system svc/kubetail-dashboard 8080:8080
Visit
http://localhost:8080
.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：政府是否应资助失败的公司，以及该公司的现状与未来前景

不同观点：
• ccppurcell 认为，该事件可能与美国政策变化或反运动趋势有关，质疑这是否是受美国反堕胎运动等类似现象影响的"反"运动的一部分，或者是否有合法的理由与美国政策相关。
• knowitnone 反对政府再次出资救助一个已经失败的公司，认为这是在浪费资金。
• pluc 强调之前在Northvolt等可再生能源项目上的投资失败，认为政府在高端可再生能源投资上会更加谨慎。
• Animats 认为，该公司将不得不依赖外部采购，例如从BYD购买产品。
• Kon-Peki 提供了一个具体的拍卖链接，指出由于美国电动车制造设施关闭，导致公司面临清算。
• mg 从环境和社会健康的角度出发，支持电动巴士的推广，认为它们能提供更舒适和安静的通勤体验。
• plorg 对该公司在贸易展上的表现持积极看法，认为其产品在某些领域有竞争力，但对该公司在当前国际政治环境下的运营能力表示担忧。
• 0xbadc0de5 坚决反对政府救助经营不善的公司，认为这只会助长不负责任的行为。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了政府资助失败企业的合理性，有人认为这是不负责任的浪费，而另一些人则关注更广泛的环境和社会效益。
• 不同评论者对该公司产品在市场中的竞争力及其在国际政治环境下的生存能力存在争议。
• 评论中还提到了美国政策变化可能对其他国家产生的连锁反应，以及这种影响是否合理或可取。

争议焦点：
• 政府是否应该救助失败的公司，尤其是那些涉及可再生能源和高风险技术领域的企业。
• 该公司在当前国际政治和市场环境下的生存能力以及未来发展前景。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby 中处理无效 UTF-8 字节序列的问题以及对 "伪支持" 的看法

不同观点：
• [kayodelycaon] 认为在 Ruby 中无法扫描包含无效 UTF-8 字节序列的字符串是一个基本常识，UTF-8 编码的字符串必须是有效的 UTF-8。这不是 Ruby 独有的问题，Python 3 也有类似行为。他通过代码示例展示了如何处理字节序列，并指出这是一个简单问题，通过搜索或询问同事很容易解决。他对该高级工程师没有自行解决这个问题表示失望。

• [yxhuvud] 表示对 "假装支持 UTF-8 匹配而实际不支持" 的行为感到不满，认为这种伪支持不美观。

• [gitroom] 赞同 [yxhuvud] 的观点，并进一步强调伪支持比完全不支持更糟糕。他认为不诚实的支持会带来更大的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于 Ruby 对无效 UTF-8 字节序列的处理是否为一个显而易见的问题，以及这种 "伪支持" 是否可以接受。
• kayodelycaon 提供了技术细节和解决方案，暗示问题可以通过适当的研究和沟通解决，而 yxhuvud 和 gitroom 更关注问题的伦理和用户体验层面。
• 对于伪支持的定义和影响，不同评论者有不同看法，但普遍认为伪支持会带来负面影响。

data.title: xAI dev leaks API key for private SpaceX, Tesla LLMs
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 一名xAI员工在GitHub上泄露了一个私人密钥，该密钥在过去两个月内可能允许任何人访问xAI的私有大型语言模型（LLM）。这些模型似乎是为处理马斯克旗下公司（如SpaceX、Tesla和Twitter/X）的内部数据而定制的。安全公司Seralys的首席黑客官Caturegli最早公开了这一泄露事件。GitGuardian的研究人员发现，该密钥可以访问xAI的多个未发布模型，包括Grok chatbot，以及一些定制的私有模型（如tweet-rejector和grok-spacex-2024-11-04）。尽管GitGuardian在两个月前就提醒了xAI员工，但密钥在被删除前仍然有效。这一事件暴露了xAI在密钥管理和内部监控方面的不足，尽管没有证据表明政府或用户数据因此被泄露，但可能无意中暴露了公司内部的开发信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：xAI的API密钥泄露事件及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [Aurornis] 认为xAI的安全团队让GitGuardian通过HackerOne的漏洞赏金计划报告问题的做法非常不妥，尽管最终有人解决了问题，但这种流程延误了处理时间。
• [mcs5280] 指出该事件可能导致严重的ITAR违规，特别是如果涉及SpaceX的数据。
• [Cheer2171] 批评xAI及其开发人员的 incompetence，认为所有组织都应持续扫描以防止API密钥泄露，而不仅仅是依赖个别开发人员。
• [breakingcups] 对私人模型"tweet-rejector"的用途更感兴趣，暗示该模型可能有其他重要应用。
• [KristenDev] 担心自己的研究因类似泄露事件而受到影响，质疑在xAI未回应的情况下应采取何种行动（如发布视频、声明或分享见解）。
• [rcarmo] 指出一些记者错误地假设拥有LMM的API密钥可以用于注入数据，认为公众对LLM的工作原理仍缺乏了解。
• [threecheese] 对政府机构监控员工通讯以寻找对总统的敌对思想表示震惊，认为异议应是健康的民主组成部分。
• [SillyUsername] 开玩笑地说，泄露API密钥的开发人员可能会被马斯克解雇。
• [jsight] 认为类似泄露事件频繁发生，举例说自己可能也曾经不小心泄露过自己的.ssh目录，暗示这是开发过程中常见的人为错误。

补充讨论：
• 关于API密钥泄露的技术和管理流程问题引发了对安全实践的广泛批评。
• 对私人模型用途的猜测显示出对技术应用的广泛兴趣和潜在担忧。
• 政府监控通讯的讨论引发了对隐私和异议价值的深层次思考。
• 对马斯克及其公司文化（如解雇行为）的调侃反映了公众对马斯克管理风格的固有印象。

43865097.article_content:
An employee at Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company
xAI
leaked a private key on
GitHub
that for the past two months could have allowed anyone to query private xAI large language models (LLMs) which appear to have been custom made for working with internal data from Musk’s companies, including
SpaceX
,
Tesla
and
Twitter/X,
KrebsOnSecurity has learned.
Image: Shutterstock, @sdx15.
Philippe Caturegli
, “chief hacking officer” at the security consultancy
Seralys
, was
the first to publicize the leak
of credentials for an x.ai application programming interface (API) exposed in the GitHub code repository of a technical staff member at xAI.
Caturegli’s post on LinkedIn caught the attention of researchers at
GitGuardian
, a company that specializes in detecting and remediating exposed secrets in public and proprietary environments. GitGuardian’s systems constantly scan GitHub and other code repositories for exposed API keys, and fire off automated alerts to affected users.
GitGuardian’s
Eric Fourrier
told KrebsOnSecurity the exposed API key had access to several unreleased models of
Grok
, the AI chatbot developed by xAI. In total, GitGuardian found the key had access to at least 60 fine-tuned and private LLMs.
“The credentials can be used to access the X.ai API with the identity of the user,” GitGuardian wrote in an email explaining their findings to xAI. “The associated account not only has access to public Grok models (grok-2-1212, etc) but also to what appears to be unreleased (grok-2.5V), development (research-grok-2p5v-1018), and private models (tweet-rejector, grok-spacex-2024-11-04).”
Fourrier found GitGuardian had alerted the xAI employee about the exposed API key nearly two months ago — on March 2. But as of April 30, when GitGuardian directly alerted xAI’s security team to the exposure, the key was still valid and usable. xAI told GitGuardian to report the matter through its bug bounty program at
HackerOne
, but just a few hours later the repository containing the API key was removed from GitHub.
“It looks like some of these internal LLMs were fine-tuned on SpaceX data, and some were fine-tuned with Tesla data,” Fourrier said. “I definitely don’t think a Grok model that’s fine-tuned on SpaceX data is intended to be exposed publicly.”
xAI did not respond to a request for comment. Nor did the 28-year-old xAI technical staff member whose key was exposed.
Carole Winqwist
, chief marketing officer at GitGuardian, said giving potentially hostile users free access to private LLMs is a recipe for disaster.
“If you’re an attacker and you have direct access to the model and the back end interface for things like Grok, it’s definitely something you can use for further attacking,” she said. “An attacker could it use for prompt injection, to tweak the (LLM) model to serve their purposes, or try to implant code into the supply chain.”
The inadvertent exposure of internal LLMs for xAI comes as Musk’s so-called
Department of Government Efficiency
(DOGE) has been feeding sensitive government records into artificial intelligence tools. In February,
The Washington Post
reported
DOGE officials were feeding data from across the Education Department into AI tools to probe the agency’s programs and spending.
The Post said DOGE plans to replicate this process across many departments and agencies, accessing the back-end software at different parts of the government and then using AI technology to extract and sift through information about spending on employees and programs.
“Feeding sensitive data into AI software puts it into the possession of a system’s operator, increasing the chances it will be leaked or swept up in cyberattacks,” Post reporters wrote.
Wired reported in March that DOGE has
deployed a proprietary chatbot called GSAi
to 1,500 federal workers at the
General Services Administration
, part of an effort to automate tasks previously done by humans as DOGE continues its purge of the federal workforce.
A
Reuters
report
last month said Trump administration officials told some U.S. government employees that DOGE is using AI to surveil at least one federal agency’s communications for hostility to President Trump and his agenda. Reuters wrote that the DOGE team has heavily deployed Musk’s Grok AI chatbot as part of their work slashing the federal government, although Reuters said it could not establish exactly how Grok was being used.
Caturegli said while there is no indication that federal government or user data could be accessed through the exposed x.ai API key, these private models are likely trained on proprietary data and may unintentionally expose details related to internal development efforts at xAI, Twitter, or SpaceX.
“The fact that this key was publicly exposed for two months and granted access to internal models is concerning,” Caturegli said. “This kind of long-lived credential exposure highlights weak key management and insufficient internal monitoring, raising questions about safeguards around deve

data.title: Don't watermark your legal PDFs with purple dragons in suits
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 联邦法官对律师在其法律PDF文件中使用巨大电子水印（如一个穿着西装的紫色卡通龙）感到不满。这一情况源于一起案件，律师Jacob A. Perrone的律所“Dragon Lawyers”在其文件中广泛使用了该卡通形象，引起法官Ray Kent的批评，称其“幼稚且不恰当”，并下令禁止再使用类似内容。尽管Perrone表示将继续使用该标志，但会在未来提交的文件中减少此类装饰。此事在法律博客社区引发了广泛讨论和调侃。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于法律文件中出现不当内容（如卡通龙）的讨论，涉及法律文件处理的专业性、文件呈现方式的适当性以及对司法过程的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持去除个性化或不当内容的观点**：
   - [mmmlinux] 建议使用类似代码检查工具的程序自动清理法律文件中可能标识个人身份的独特内容，以确保文件的标准化和匿名性。
   - [apparent] 强调法院对文件格式有严格要求，无法理解为何律师会认为包含卡通龙的文件能通过审核。

• **关注案件背景及受害人处境的观点**：
   - [perihelions] 认为整个事件比卡通龙更令人不安的是，案件中的原告因缺乏法律资源而不得不接受不专业的法律服务。这反映了司法系统中的不平等问题。

• **关于语言使用和表达方式的观点**：
   - [OJFord] 质疑在标题或首段使用具体事物（如卡通龙），然后在后续段落中强行使用同义词的写作风格，认为这种做法不自然且可能令人困惑。

• **关于文件视觉设计的观点**：
   - [mjgoeke] 指出文件中的“水印”问题，认为保持5%的透明度是标准，而13%的透明度过于显眼且分散注意力。
   - [goku12] 认为法官对卡通龙水印的反应可以理解，自己也难以接受如此显眼的视觉元素。
   - [generationP] 提到跨页水印的使用目前尚未找到比页边注释更有效的用途，且影响文件的可读性和兼容性。

• **关于测试数据和开发者习惯的观点**：
   - [wiradikusuma] 作为开发者分享了在测试数据中使用虚构角色（如蝙蝠侠、猫图片）的习惯，以便明确区分测试数据，但承认某些客户对这种做法不满意。
   - [neilv] 提到在草稿文件中使用大水印（如“草稿”）的做法，认为卡通龙可能只是律师内部审查草稿时用作轻松减压的一种方式。

• **对司法系统正式性和幽默感的看法**：
   - [brumar] 对法院文件中出现卡通龙后的正式回应感到有趣，认为这是“正式回应荒唐事”的例子。
   - [zahrc] 质疑法院认为卡通龙“幼稚且不合适”的观点，将其比作长辈在餐桌上训斥年轻人，认为司法系统不应过于严肃。

• **关于司法偏见和个人表达的观点**：
   - [demarq] 提出司法过程应基于案件本身而非个人偏见，质疑如果有人带着纹身出庭是否会被认为更有罪，反映了司法过程中的潜在偏见。

• **关于法律文件中品牌标识和水印的合法性问题**：
   - [cookingmyserver] 询问法律文件中使用水印和律师事务所标识是否常见及合法，提出了对法律文件标准和规范的疑问。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及幽默感和严肃性之间的平衡问题，尤其是在法律文件中出现不寻常元素时。
- 讨论了开发者在测试环境中使用虚构数据的习惯及其潜在影响。
- 涉及司法系统中对格式和内容严格要求的重要性以及可能存在的偏见问题。

Being a model citizen and a person of taste, you probably don't
need
this reminder, but some others do: Federal judges do not like it when lawyers electronically watermark every page of their legal PDFs with a gigantic image—
purchased for $20 online
—of a purple dragon wearing a suit and tie. Not even if your firm's name is "Dragon Lawyers."
Federal Magistrate Judge Ray Kent of the Western District of Michigan was unamused by a
recent complaint
(PDF) that prominently featured the aubergine wyrm.
"Each page of plaintiff’s complaint appears on an e-filing which is dominated by a large multi-colored cartoon dragon dressed in a suit," he
wrote on April 28
(PDF). "Use of this dragon cartoon logo is not only distracting, it is juvenile and impertinent. The Court is not a cartoon."
Kent then ordered "that plaintiff shall not file any other documents with the cartoon dragon or other inappropriate content."
Seriously, don't do this.
The unusual order generated coverage across the legal blogging community, which was apparently
ensorcelled
by a spell requiring headline writers to use dragon-related puns, including:
Judge Slays Dragon-Branded Lawyer’s Marketing Effort
Magistrate judge is breathing fire over law firm's dragon logo on legal pleadings
Exit the Dragon
US judge gives fiery response to e-filing “dominated by large cartoon dragon dressed in a suit”
Jacob A. Perrone is the lawyer behind Dragon Lawyers (phone number: [area code redacted] JAKELAW). His
website
, which also features the purple dragon and a bunch of busted links in the footer, says that the firm "integrates AI to lower the cost of legal services."
The New York Times
got in touch with Perrone this week
, who explained that he liked
Game of Thrones
, that he bought the dragon image online, and that he selected it because "people like dragons." He plans to keep using the logo but will tone it down in future filings.
The whole story would be far more humorous were it not from a case in which Perrone represented a woman who claims that she nearly died after being incarcerated and not given proper medical care. Perrone must now refile his complaint in that case—without the cartoon dragon.
Nate Anderson

Nate Anderson
Deputy Editor
Nate is the deputy editor at Ars Technica. His most recent book is
In Emergency, Break Glass: What Nietzsche Can Teach Us About Joyful Living in a Tech-Saturated World
, which is much funnier than it sounds.

data.title: Bloom Filters
data.author: mfrw
data.article_summary:
Bloom filters是一种用于高效集合成员检查的概率数据结构，由Burton Bloom在1970年提出，旨在通过概率方法减少时间和空间开销，特别适用于需要频繁判断元素是否不属于某个集合的场景。其主要特点是：如果Bloom filter判断某个元素不在集合中，则结果必定为真；但如果判断元素在集合中，则可能存在假阳性。

Bloom filter由一个位数组和多个哈希函数组成。插入元素时，使用k个哈希函数将元素映射到位数组的多个位置，并将这些位置设为1。检查元素是否在集合中时，再次使用k个哈希函数，若对应位置全为1，则可能存在（假阳性）；若有任何一个位置为0，则元素必定不在集合中。

该结构非常适合磁盘读取等需要大量负查询的场景，因其快速和节省空间的特性被广泛应用。
